0 stops the Thruster, 15 gives full thrust, and everything in between scales proportionally.
createthrusters.ponder.thruster_basics.t: A Thruster pushes its contraption away from the nozzle, with redstone controlling how much force it produces.
Lower signals give less thrust, so increase the signal when you need more power.
Mount the Thruster on a Servo Bearing if you need to redirect that force while flying.
createthrusters.ponder.thruster_propulsi: Thrusters consume fuel while they're running, with redstone strength 0 to 15 controlling their output.
Load Coal, Blaze Rods, Lava, or any other supported fuel. Installing a Thruster Lens replaces fuel with FE.
Propulsion Upgrades increase thrust and fuel consumption together, so make sure the fuel supply can keep up.
createthrusters.ponder.thruster_processi: Install a Processing Upgrade and place Depots in the exhaust to Smoke, Smelt, or Haunt the items on them.
Higher tiers process faster and reach further, but the extra work also increases fuel consumption.
Processing also works in Focused Mode, with higher tiers increasing the beam's processing range and speed.
createthrusters.ponder.thruster_control_: Each Thruster can use Auto, Redstone, or Computer control.
Minimum and maximum throttle limits let you keep every input inside the range you actually want the Thruster to use.
ComputerCraft can set the throttle and control mode, enable or disable the Thruster, and read its current state.
createthrusters.ponder.thruster_dynamic_: At its simplest, a Thruster only needs fuel and a redstone signal to produce thrust.
Add a Processing Upgrade and the exhaust can process recipes as well, consuming extra fuel while it works.
Use whichever control mode fits the build: automatic input, redstone, or direct computer control.
createthrusters.ponder.thruster.propulsi: How to Fuel and Fire a Thruster
A fueled Thruster generates force away from its nozzle.
For continuous operation, keep liquid fuel supplied through a pipe.
Coal, Blaze Rods, Blaze Cakes, and other supported solid fuels can also be loaded directly into the Thruster.
Redstone controls the throttle: 0 stops it completely and 15 runs it at full output.
At signal strength 15 the Thruster produces all of its available thrust.
Lower signals scale that output proportionally, so signal 8 is roughly half thrust.
Put a Create Filter in the filter slot if you want to disable the sound and exhaust plume.
The filter only hides those effects; the Thruster itself keeps working normally.
Dye can be applied directly to the Thruster to change the exhaust colour.
Set the signal back to 0 whenever you want the Thruster to stop.
Sneak + Use the Thruster to open its settings.
From here you can limit its throttle range, choose a control mode, and install upgrades.
Every Propulsion Upgrade tier doubles the previous tier's thrust, reaching 16x normal thrust at Tier 4.
The filter slot accepts a Create Filter, letting you disable the plume and sound without disabling the Thruster.
Installing a Thruster Lens enables Focused Mode, replacing normal fuel with FE.
In Focused Mode all operating power is drawn from a connected FE cable.
As long as the cable can supply enough FE, the Thruster can keep running.
Apply redstone to fire the focused energy beam.
Dye changes the beam colour the same way it changes normal exhaust.
Remove the Lens to switch the Thruster back to normal fuel.
createthrusters.ponder.thruster.processi: Using the Thruster as a Processing Station
A Processing Upgrade lets the Thruster's exhaust process recipes on items placed in front of it.
Smoking cooks food. Put raw food on a Depot inside the exhaust and let the Thruster do the rest.
Any supported food is replaced with its cooked result once processing finishes.
Smelting works the same way, but uses normal furnace recipes instead.
For example, Raw Iron placed in the exhaust becomes an Iron Ingot.
Haunting uses the exhaust for Soul Fire recipes instead.
For example, Gravel becomes Soul Sand after being Haunted.
Higher tiers increase processing speed and range. Filters can hide the plume, and Focused Mode works for larger processing setups.
Steering a Servo Bearing
Pointing a Bearing with the Contraption Controller
A Servo Bearing rotates its mounted assembly, letting attached Thrusters point their force in a different direction.
The Contraption Controller can send target angles directly to the bearing, so Redstone Links aren't required.
The controller decides where the bearing should point, while shaft speed decides how quickly it gets there.
Feed it a Joystick for manual steering, or orientation data when you want the bearing to correct itself.
Steering with a Joystick and Advanced Data Link
An Advanced Data Link can connect the bearing to a Joystick or another orientation source.
Moving the Joystick then becomes a live target angle for the bearing.
The bearing follows that target smoothly, giving you direct analogue steering.
For automatic control, replace the Joystick with a Gimbal Sensor and use Servo Mode.
Automatic Bearing Control with Servo Mode
Servo Mode lets a Smart Gearbox hold the bearing at an exact target angle.
Connect an orientation source and its live reading becomes that target.
As the reading changes, the bearing follows it toward the new angle.
This gives you a feedback loop you can use for flight controls that automatically correct tilt.
Passing Fuel Through a Servo Bearing
Connect a fluid pipe or FE cable below the Servo Bearing to supply whatever is mounted above it.
Liquid fuel can pass straight through the bearing into a tank on the moving assembly.
The same connection can carry either liquid fuel or FE across the rotating joint.
Mounted Thrusters stay supplied while the bearing moves them to a new angle.
Use an FE cable instead of a pipe when those Thrusters are running in Focused Mode.
Break the pipe or cable and the supply stops until you reconnect it.
createthrusters.ponder.claw.basics.text_: Hang the Claw below a Rope Winch by using rope on the Winch.
You can also use the Winch while holding the Claw; rope is taken from your inventory.
Open the Claw settings with Sneak + Use, then assign its Redstone Link frequency.
A closed Claw searches below itself for a Rope Connector on a contraption.
Signal the assigned frequency to close the Claw and lift the matching connector.
Remove the signal to open the Claw and release its load.
createthrusters.ponder.bidirectional_gea: A Smart Gearbox carries independent East/West and North/South rotation through one block.
Rotation entering the East face leaves through the West face without changing speed.
The North/South lane can use a different speed and direction without mixing with East/West.
Each lane has its own stress budget, which keeps compact multi-axis builds practical.
Use a face to invert that output when two bearings need opposite directions.
Passthrough Mode keeps both lanes active and ignores sensor or computer targets.
Servo Mode turns the four face outputs toward angles supplied by live orientation data.
Put an Advanced Data Link on top and connect it to a Gimbal Sensor or another orientation source.
The gearbox uses that tilt reading to calculate a corrective angle for every output.
Each face gives its Servo Bearing a separate target, with shaft speed controlling how fast it moves.
All four bearings correct their own axes together, keeping the craft level while it moves.
ComputerCraft scripts can override any face separately with setFaceAngle().
createthrusters.ponder.variable_transmis: The Variable Transmission scales its input speed with redstone before passing rotation to the output.
Signal 0 stops the output without stopping the input shaft.
Signal 8 produces roughly half of the input speed.
Signal 15 passes the full input speed through.
createthrusters.ponder.analogue_joystick: Tilting the Analogue Joystick produces a separate 0 to 15 redstone signal on each side.
The faces map to movement: North is Forward, South is Backward, East is Right, and West is Left.
Greater tilt produces a stronger signal, reaching 15 at the movement limit.
Both axes combine, so diagonal stick movement produces forward and sideways signals together.
Open the Joystick settings with Sneak + Use.
Configure its deadzone, tilt limit, and whether it returns to center after release.
Momentary Mode returns every signal to 0 when the stick is released.
Latched Mode keeps the last position, which is useful for a throttle that must stay set.
createthrusters.ponder.analogue_contrapt: The Sable Contraption Controller provides 13 key-bound channels with wireless redstone output.
Assign a Redstone Link frequency to broadcast one channel to its wireless receiver.
A Nixie Tube on the receiving side makes the channel's live signal easy to check.
Use the controller to bind keys for Pitch, Roll, Yaw, Throttle, and the other channels.
Ramp Mode raises the signal gradually while its key remains held.
Step Mode changes the signal by a fixed amount on every key press for precise adjustments.
Latch Mode uses one press to enable the channel and the next to disable it.
An input frequency can feed Joystick movement straight into a channel.
Input and output frequencies stay independent, preventing a signal from feeding back into itself.
Send a channel to a Servo Bearing frequency to steer it from the controller.
The bearing follows the Joystick signal and turns the mounted Thruster with it.
Insert a Contraption Network Linker to bind blocks without wireless frequencies.
Use a redstone-controlled block with the Linker to add that block as a target.
Any controller channel can then operate the bound block directly.
createthrusters.ponder.physics_gantry.ba: Physics Gantry Shafts form the track, carry rotation, and keep the Carriage on a straight path.
Extend the track with shaft segments that share the same facing and meet end to end.
Mount the Physics Gantry Carriage on a side face with its front pointing away from the shaft.
Shaft rotation moves the Carriage and powers the machinery attached to its outer face.
Link Physics Gantry Belt Wheels to carry rotation between fixed and moving assemblies.
The Belt Wheel keeps turning while the Carriage moves, so its attached machinery stays powered.
A moving belt appears after both endpoints are linked and shows the active power path.

block.createthrusters.alternator.tooltip: Turns shaft rotation into FE. More RPM means more power, but also more stress on the kinetic network.
No power is generated below the minimum speed. Above that, output increases with RPM.
The alternator stores power internally. Connect a cable to any face to draw from it.

item.createthrusters.processing_upgrade_: Processing Upgrade: Smoking Tier 1
Adds smoke processing to the thruster's exhaust. Food placed on nearby Depots will be cooked.
Processing Upgrade: Smelting Tier 1
Adds smelting to the thruster's exhaust. Raw ores and other smeltable items on nearby Depots will be processed.
Processing Upgrade: Haunting Tier 1
Infuses the exhaust with soul fire. Items on nearby Depots will undergo haunting transformations.
Processing Upgrade: Smoking Tier 2
Smokes items in the exhaust faster than Tier 1.
Processing Upgrade: Smelting Tier 2
Smelts items in the exhaust faster than Tier 1.
Processing Upgrade: Haunting Tier 2
Haunts items in the exhaust faster than Tier 1.
Processing Upgrade: Smoking Tier 3
Faster smoking than Tier 2, with a wider effective area.
Processing Upgrade: Smelting Tier 3
Faster smelting than Tier 2, with a wider effective area.
Processing Upgrade: Haunting Tier 3
Faster haunting than Tier 2, with a wider effective area.
Processing Upgrade: Smoking Tier 4
The fastest and most powerful smoking upgrade. Maximum range and processing speed.
Processing Upgrade: Smelting Tier 4
The fastest and most powerful smelting upgrade. Maximum range and processing speed.
Processing Upgrade: Haunting Tier 4
The fastest and most powerful haunting upgrade. Maximum range and processing speed.

createthrusters.ponder.industrial_altern: Generating Power with the Industrial Alternator
The Industrial Alternator turns shaft rotation into FE.
Higher RPM increases both FE output and the stress placed on the kinetic network.
Run Andesite Cables from any face to supply FE machines with the generated power.
Converting Power with the Industrial Motor
The Industrial Motor consumes FE to drive a shaft, reversing the Alternator's conversion.
A higher target RPM requires more FE while the Motor is running.
Hold Use and drag across the Motor's back face to choose its target RPM.
